questions.q: The heat of combustion of ethanol into carbon dioxides and water is $- 327$~Kcal at constant pressure. The heat evolved (in cal) at constant volume at~$27 ° C$ (if all gases behave ideally) is  \left(R = 2{calmol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}\right)________
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${C}_{2}{H}_{5}OH ( ℓ ) + {O}_{2} ( g ) ⟶ 2{O}_{2} ( g ) + 3{H}_{2}O ( ℓ ) ; \Delta{H}_{C} = - 327Kcal$
$\Delta Hc = \Delta{U}_{C} + \Delta{n}_{g}RT$
$- 327 \times {10}^{3} = \Delta{U}_{C} + 1 \times 2 \times 300$
$\Delta{U}_{C} = - 326400cal$

So heat evolved as constant volume is~$326400$cal&

questions.q: Enthalpies of formation of ${CCl}_{4} ( g ) , {H}_{2}O ( g ) , {CO}_{2} ( g )$ and $HCl$ are $- 105, - 242, - 394$~and $- 92kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ respectively. The magnitude of enthalpy of the reaction given below is ${kJmol}^{- 1}$. (nearest integer) ${CCl}_{4} ( g ) + 2{H}_{2}O ( g ) \to {CO}_{2} ( g ) + 4HCl ( g )$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Using Hess's law of constant heat summation:
Enthalpy of reaction = Enthalpy of formation of products - Enthalpy of formation of reactants
$∴ {ΔH}_{f} ° = {ΔH}_{f} ° \left({CO}_{2}, g\right) + 4{ΔH}_{f} ° ( HCl ) - {ΔH}_{f} ° \left({CCl}_{4}\right) -2{ΔH}_{f} ° \left({H}_{2}O, r\right)$

$= [ - 394 ] + 4 [ - 92 ] + 105 - 2 \times [242 ]$

$= - 394 - 368 + 105 + 484$

$= - 173kJ / mole

$

Consider the following reaction at $298K$.

$\dfrac{3}{2}{O}_{2\left(g\right)} ⇌ {O}_{3\left(g\right)} . {K}_{p} = 2 . 47 \times {10}^{- 29}$

${∆}_{r}G^{0}$ for the reaction is _________ $kJ$. (Given $R = 8 . 314{JK}^{– 1}{mol}^{– 1}$)

Round off your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given $R = 8 . 314{JK}^{– 1}{mol}^{– 1}$

$\dfrac{3}{2}{O}_{2\left(g\right)} ⇌ {O}_{3\left(g\right)} . {K}_{p} = 2 . 47 \times {10}^{- 29}$

Standard Gibbs free energy of the formation of a compound is basically the change of Gibbs free energy that is followed by the formation of one mole of that substance from its component element available at their standard states or the most stable form of the element which is at $25 ° C$ and $100$ kPa. Its symbol is ${Δ}_{f}G ˚$.

${∆}_{r}G^{0} = - RTln{K}_{p}$

$= - 8 . 314 \times {10}^{– 3} \times 298 \times \ln ( 2 . 47 \times {10}^{– 29} )$

$= – 8 . 314 \times {10}^{– 3} \times 298 \times ( – 65 . 87 )$

$= 163 . 19kJ$

questions.q:
$28 . 0$ L of ${CO}_{2}$~is produced on complete combustion of $16 . 8L$ gaseous mixture of ethene and methane at $25 ° C$ and $1$ atm. Heat evolved during the combustion process is $kJ$

Given$: {ΔH}_{C}\left({CH}_{4}\right) = - 900kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

${ΔH}_{C}\left({C}_{2}{H}_{4}\right) = - 1400kJ{mol}^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Complete combustion of ethene& and methane mixture produces carbon dioxide.
Let, Volume of ${C}_{2}{H}_{4}$~is $x$ litre

${C}_{2}{H}_{4} + 3{O}_{2} \to 2{CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Initial volume of carbon dioxide 0
Final~volume of carbon dioxide~$2x$

${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} \to {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Initial volume of carbon dioxide is 0

Final~volume of carbon dioxide~is~$( 16 . 8 - x )$

Total volume of~${CO}_{2} = 2x + 16 . 8 - x$

$⇒ 28 = 16 . 8 + x$

$x = 11 . 2L$

${n}_{CH4} = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{1 \times 5 . 6}{0 . 082 \times 298} = 0 . 229mole$

${n}_{{C}_{2}{H}_{4}} = \dfrac{11 . 2}{0 . 082 \times 298} = 0 . 458mole$

$∴$ Heat evolved using standard enthalpy of combustion~$= 0 . 229 \times 900 + 0 . 458 \times 1400$

$= 206 . 1 + 641 . 2$

$= 847 . 3kJ$

questions.q:
The incorrect statements from the following is:
A.& The electrical work that a reaction can perform at constant pressure and temperature is equal to the reaction Gibbs energy.
B.& ${E}_{cell}^{∘}$~ is dependent on the pressure.
C.~${dE}_{cell}^{°}dT = \dfrac{{Δ}_{r}S^{°}}{nF}$
D. A cell is operating reversibly if the cell potential is exactly balanced by an opposing source of potential difference.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${E}_{cell}^{∘}$~is dependent on the equilibrium constant, $K$,~which is~not dependent on the pressure of any gas involved in the cell.~Relation between Electrochemical Cell Potential and Gibbs free Energy change is given by; $\Delta G = - nFE$ where Delta G is Gibbs Free energy change , n is the number of electrons involved in the reaction and F is Faraday and E is the Cell potential.

We know that,

$dG = VdP - SdT$

At constant pressure~$dP = 0$

$⇒ dG = - SdT$

$S = - \dfrac{dG}{dT} ∆ S = - \left(\dfrac{∆ \left(dG\right)}{dT}\right)P$

$⇒ {dE}_{cell}^{°}dT = \dfrac{∆ S}{nF}$

A cell is operating reversibly if the cell potential is exactly balanced by an opposing source of potential difference.

questions.q: A gas ( Molar mass $= 280g{mol}^{- 1}$) was burnt in excess ${O}_{2}$ in a constant volume calorimeter and during combustion the temperature of calorimeter increased from $298 . 0K$ to $298 . 45K$. If the heat capacity of calorimeter is $2 . 5kJK^{- 1}$ and enthalpy of combustion of gas is $9kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ then amount of gas burnt is____g.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Let $xg$~is burnt

Moles$= \dfrac{x}{280}$~heat released by~$\dfrac{x}{280}mole = 2 . 5 \times 0 . 45kJ$ heat released by $1$~mole~$= \dfrac{2 . 5 \times 0 . 45 \times 280}{x}kJ$

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta ngRT$

$\Delta H ≃ \Delta U$

$9 = \dfrac{2 . 5 \times 280 \times 0 . 45}{x}$

$x = 35g$
